adoption_rule: (a) rerender_consistent detection, counted as tampered or suspicious, on dev rises by at least 10 percentage points over the old version
(b) an anomaly score alone can never produce 'tampered'
(c) the 'tampered' false-alarm rate on genuine dev and on resaved_genuine is unchanged from the old version
dev_adoption.decision: v2 is adopted: all three conditions hold

expectations: These are what dev showed, written down before test is opened. They are not targets and nothing is tuned to them.
dev, rule v2: rerender_inconsistent, inplace_edit, page_swap and page_remove 60/60 flagged each; inplace_edit_consistent 59/60; rerender_consistent 7/60 (11.7%, interval 5-20%), tampered 0/60.

dev false alarms: 'tampered' 0/300 on genuine dev and 0/60 on resaved_genuine; 'tampered or suspicious' 6/300 (2.0%) on genuine dev and 1/60 on resaved_genuine; 0/300 flagged on genuine dev without anomaly findings.

So on test: most types expected near 100% flagged, rerender_consistent expected low, tampered false alarms expected near zero, and 'suspicious' on genuine expected near 2% (the anomaly threshold's rate).
overlay: no expectation. It is held out and dev has no overlay data.
shift: 'tampered' expected near 0; flagged (tampered or suspicious) rate may exceed 2% because the anomaly model never saw this distribution; no number pre-stated.
Anything far from this is reported as it is.
known_limits: The anomaly check's false-alarm rate on genuine dev and genuine train is in-sample (its threshold and model came from those statements); only test and shift are independent.
v2 was adopted on dev with a thin margin on condition (a): rerender_consistent rose from 0/60 to 7/60, 11.7 points against 10 needed.
All of v2's rerender_consistent gains come from the anomaly score alone, whose threshold is in-sample on dev.
Two anomaly features (income_to_debits and salary_to_spending) depend indirectly on the Week 3 salary rule, through the profile; the anomaly check can never give 'tampered' on its own.
The layout tolerances and the font baseline were measured on genuine train, so the zero strong findings on genuine dev and train are not independent evidence.

The in-table character-overlap maximum on genuine PDFs was never recorded; only that no genuine dev or train PDF produced a strong finding, so the margin to the 0.30 threshold is not shown. This measurement cannot change a verdict.
There is no test for a header mismatch on the drcr layout (only on columns). A missing test cannot change a verdict.

Populations are identified by statement id and by the PDF hash recorded by each run, not checked against the generator; shift PDFs copied to another folder would be caught only through their overlap with the test ids.
The pooled all-six-types rate hides the rerender_consistent gap and is not a headline.
Dev copies are 60 per type; test is 100 per type, so test intervals are narrower.
metrics: detection per tamper type, counted as 'tampered' and as 'tampered or suspicious', each with a 95% bootstrap interval (1,000 resamples over source statements)
the same two counts with every file-history finding removed
the save-mode breakdown (incremental vs full rewrite) for the types a PDF library wrote, including resaved_genuine
per-type finding-code counts: on how many copies each strong and each weak code fired
the layout breakdown (columns vs drcr) as count/total and percent, no intervals; gaps over 15 points flagged, small counts noted
false alarms on genuine test: 'tampered', and 'tampered or suspicious', with and without anomaly findings
false alarms on genuine shift, and on the resaved_genuine copies

'could not check' (a check crashed and no evidence was found): its own count for every group, tampered copies and genuine alike, never counted as no evidence; and per check, on how many PDFs each check crashed
the per-copy CSV reports/week6_tamper_test_copies.csv (copy, type, layout, save mode, verdict, first check), committed
overlay: reported separately, not pooled with the six types
rules: test and shift are each scored once, after this file is committed and pushed

nothing in src/statementscreen, the model, uv.lock or the verdict rules changes after this commit; score_tamper refuses to score if anything differs, and it compares with the pushed version of this file, not the working-tree copy
no retuning after seeing test results; a bug found is reported as a finding, not fixed silently
test numbers are reported next to the dev numbers, never blended with them
a re-run is reported next to the first result and labelled post-hoc
If the builder cannot reach 100 copies for any type, it exits and we STOP and report the shortfall. No change to seed, count or code. Any re-run with a reduced count is labelled post-hoc.

score_tamper identifies populations by what they contain and what each run records, not by the name typed on the command line: the recorded population must match; test must be exactly the test statements and shift exactly the shift batch from its own folder; no other population may contain a test statement (ids are unique only within a batch: the shift batch reuses ids of the main batch, so it is identified by its source folder and its manifest ids); test copies must be built only from test statements, with seed 6; a --limit run is never scored; 300 genuine test, 300 shift and 800 copies (100 of each of eight types) are required, each PDF with a recorded SHA-256; an incomplete build is refused. tamper.run also refuses to read test PDFs without --split test (or --population test) and STATEMENTSCREEN_OPEN_TEST=1. Statements are identified by id and PDF hash as recorded by the run, not checked against the generator.

The test report and the per-copy CSV (required with the copies) are written once and never overwritten (--overwrite is refused, and a path that git has ever recorded cannot be written again, so deleting a committed result does not allow a second first result). Any later run uses --post-hoc, writes its own file with post_hoc in its name, and is labelled post-hoc.

Inputs created at step 6 (the test keys, the build summary, the detector runs and their PDFs) cannot be hashed now: their seeds are recorded above, and their SHA-256 hashes, a combined hash of all PDFs per run, and the upstream commit hash are written into the test report.

Crashes, per check: a check that crashes on a PDF leaves only that check unrun. Any strong finding still gives 'tampered' and a weak verdict stands; otherwise a crashed check turns 'no evidence of tampering' into 'could not check', reported in its own column for tampered copies and genuine PDFs. Crashes are counted per check. A PDF the parser cannot parse keeps the earlier rule (PARSE_FAILED alone is 'suspicious').

The final registered step logs the scoring run to the local MLflow store (detector fingerprint, pre-registration commit hash, all metrics, and the report and per-copy CSV as artifacts). It runs after scoring, only reads the report, and does not change any result.

Test statements were opened in Week 5 for profile and label scoring, and the shift batch was scored in Weeks 4 and 5. The Week 6 detector has never been run on either, and no tampered copies of them exist before step 6.

seeds.anomaly_model: IsolationForest seed 42, already fitted and frozen (models/week6_iforest.pkl)
seeds.bootstrap: numpy default_rng(2026), 1,000 resamples over source statements (scoring.BOOTSTRAP_SEED)
seeds.source_draw: numpy default_rng([6, 0]): the seeded order of source statements, alternating layouts (--seed 6, the same seed as the dev set)
seeds.tamper: numpy default_rng([6, 1 + the type's position in TYPES]) per type draws each copy's seed; tamper_copy then uses default_rng([copy seed, type position])

sets.genuine_shift: the registered shift batch data/week4_shift_n300 (its own manifest), unmodified
sets.genuine_test: the split_v1 test statements of data/week1_n2000, unmodified
sets.test_copies: 800 tampered copies built from the split_v1 test statements of data/week1_n2000: 100 per type for the six types (rerender_inconsistent, rerender_consistent, inplace_edit, inplace_edit_consistent, page_swap, page_remove), 100 resaved_genuine (the re-save control) and 100 overlay (held out)

stop_rule: STOP means: if any genuine PDF has a strong finding, score_tamper prints STOP and exits with code 3. Stop, report it, and change nothing. Any later re-run is labelled post-hoc and reported next to the first result.
